newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids again hold steady with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids again hold steady with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly were unchanged again Friday despite cheap gas and waning East Coast utility demand, still underpinned by steady crude and relatively tight prompt avails, sources said.
"Natural gas is obviously the fuel of choice, but prompt supply is still tight," said one cash trader, adding firm crude also recently has buoyed resid.

In New York Harbor, prompt one percent held steady at $18.50-75 a barrel, with October paper also pegged little changed at about $19. November paper was talked 20 cents weaker in the $18.85-19.10 area, traders said.
NYH high sulphurs also were unchanged, with 2.2 percent still at $17.00-25.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, three percent notionally edged up slightly to the $16.75-17.00 area, while one percent remained talked near $17, traders said.
With little demand on the horizon and gas still cheap, most expected fuel oil to remain on the defensive near-term.
New York city gate swing gas prices slipped about five cents Friday to the $2.05-2.10/mmBtu area versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.96/mmBtu equivalent.
